title: [Bug]: DockerComposeContainer with healthcheck wait strategy fails for successive tests
body:

Core

### Testcontainers version

1.19.0

### Using the latest Testcontainers version?

Yes

### Host OS

### Host Arch

### What happened?

Consider this setup:
`docker-compose.yml`
```
version: "3.9"
services:
  oracle-db:
    image: liantisit/gvenzl-oracle-xe:18-slim
    ports:
      - "1521:1521"
    environment:
      - ORACLE_PASSWORD=phoenix
    volumes:
      - ./sql:/container-entrypoint-initdb.d
    healthcheck:
      test: [ "CMD", "/opt/oracle/healthcheck.sh" ]
      interval: 2s
```
`DockerComposeIntegrationTest.java`
```
package be.liantis.medical.followup.removeme;

import org.springframework.boot.test.context.SpringBootTest;
import org.springframework.test.context.ActiveProfiles;
import org.testcontainers.containers.DockerComposeContainer;
import org.testcontainers.containers.wait.strategy.Wait;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Container;
import org.testcontainers.junit.jupiter.Testcontainers;

import java.io.File;
import java.time.Duration;

@SpringBootTest
@ActiveProfiles("docker")
@Testcontainers
public abstract class DockerComposeIntegrationTest {

    @Container
    public static final DockerComposeContainer DOCKER_COMPOSE_CONTAINER;

    static {
        DOCKER_COMPOSE_CONTAINER = new DockerComposeContainer<>(new File("docker/lala/docker-compose.yml"))
                .withLocalCompose(true)
                .waitingFor("oracle-db", Wait.forHealthcheck().withStartupTimeout(Duration.ofMinutes(5)));
        DOCKER_COMPOSE_CONTAINER.start();
    }

}
```
`FirstIntegrationTest.java`
```
public class FirstIntegrationTest extends DockerComposeIntegrationTest {

    @Test
    void test_one() {
        System.err.println("Lala");
    }

}
```
`SecondIntegrationTest.java`
```
public class SecondIntegrationTest extends DockerComposeIntegrationTest {

    @Test
    void test_two() {
        System.err.println("Lala");
    }

}
```
When I run the suite where these two test classes are present the second one will fail to start.
The tests are in JUnit 5.
See additional information for more in depth info on what I think is going wrong.
**Note** The code and logs are adjusted slightly because of company policy
Logging is set to TRACE

### Additional Information

When I dove a bit deeper I noticed the wait strategy was still checking on an old container id (the container from the first test).
In `ContainerState.java`
![image](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/assets/11025460/18921e54-81e1-4de8-b84f-55fdf1fafb88)
and in `DockerComposeContainer.java` we do this:
```
    private void createServiceInstance(Container container) {
        String serviceName = getServiceNameFromContainer(container);
        final ComposeServiceWaitStrategyTarget containerInstance = new ComposeServiceWaitStrategyTarget(
            dockerClient,
            container,
            ambassadorContainer,
            ambassadorPortMappings.getOrDefault(serviceName, new HashMap<>())
        );

        String containerId = containerInstance.getContainerId();
        if (tailChildContainers) {
            followLogs(containerId, new Slf4jLogConsumer(log).withPrefix(container.getNames()[0]));
        }
        //follow logs using registered consumers for this service
        logConsumers
            .getOrDefault(serviceName, Collections.emptyList())
            .forEach(consumer -> followLogs(containerId, consumer));
        serviceInstanceMap.putIfAbsent(serviceName, containerInstance);
    }
```
Where `serviceInstanceMap.putIfAbsent(serviceName, containerInstance);` should probably be `serviceInstanceMap.put(serviceName, containerInstance);` since the containerInstance could be a new container?

Because of this any wait strategy that involves the container itself (f.e. forSuccessfulCommand as well) will fail.

### Workaround

I fixed this with a hacky fix by clearing `serviceInstanceMap` after each test via reflection, so by adding this to my 

For versions older than 1.19:
DockerComposeIntegrationTest
```
    @AfterAll
    public static void afterAll() throws NoSuchFieldException, IllegalAccessException {
        Field privateField = DockerComposeContainer.class.getDeclaredField("serviceInstanceMap");
        privateField.setAccessible(true);
        privateField.set(DOCKER_COMPOSE_CONTAINER, new ConcurrentHashMap<>());
    }
```
and after 1.19
```
    @AfterAll
    public static void afterAll() {
        Object field = ReflectionTestUtils.getField(DOCKER_COMPOSE_CONTAINER, "composeDelegate");
        ReflectionTestUtils.setField(field, "serviceInstanceMap", new ConcurrentHashMap<>());
    }
```
